mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate of 0.65% is below the historical average of 2.5%, indicating an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the risk-free rate and increases equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical average federal funds rate is 2.5% (1954-2017)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when FEDFUNDS < 1% over the 5-year lookback period.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.7% (current level) signals the start of a monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.7% in the last 30 days
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 0.7% over the 5-year lookback period.

mechanism_narrative: When the labor market is strengthening (PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling), it signals robust economic growth that leads to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns, as the market prices in continued expansion without immediate inflationary pressure.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in 3 months and UNRATE falls > 0.2pp in 3 months
evidence_refs: fact:Current PAYEMS is 145554.0 (thousands) and UNRATE is 4.8% (as of 2017-01)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in 3 months and UNRATE falls > 0.2pp in 3 months over the 5-year lookback period.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of high housing starts (HOUST) and strong residential fixed investment (RSAFS) signals a late-cycle expansion, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to overvaluation and the risk of monetary tightening.
evidence_refs: fact:Current HOUST is 1226.0 (Dec 2016) and RSAFS is 472142.0 (Jan 2017)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when HOUST > 1200 and RSAFS > 450000 over the 5-year lookback period.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 104.0 (current level) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors shift to safer assets.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when INDPRO falls below 104.0 over the 5-year lookback period.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of housing starts (HOUST) at 1226.0 (thousands of units) is above the 5-year average of 1100, indicating strong demand for housing and a robust economy, which leads to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when HOUST > 1100 over the 5-year lookback period.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of industrial production (INDPRO) at 104.55 (index 2017=100) is above the 2016 average of 103.0, indicating a growing industrial sector and economic expansion, which leads to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when INDPRO > 103.0 over the 5-year lookback period.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% (current level) signals a tightening labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when UNRATE < 4.5% over the 5-year lookback period.
